summary: This PR introduces several concerning changes: debug/test code left in production files (testing.ts, proxy.ts), a major layout restructuring in page.tsx that likely breaks infinite scroll detection, and a syntax issue in layout.tsx with a leading space in className.

accepted.title: Debug test file committed to production code
accepted.message: This file contains only `console.log("apple")` and appears to be a test/debug artifact. It will execute on import and pollute production logs. This should not be committed.

accepted.title: Layout restructuring likely breaks infinite scroll detection
accepted.message: The main element lost `flex items-center justify-center` and gained nested `h-full` divs. The ReelFeed is now inside `h-full flex justify-center` wrapper. Since `containerRef` is attached to ReelFeed's internal scroll container, but the page now uses `overflow-hidden` on main with nested full-height flex containers, the scroll event detection in `handleScroll` may not fire correctly. The old layout centered the feed in a flex container that could scroll; the new layout constrains height differently.
accepted.suggestion: Verify scroll behavior works with new structure. Consider restoring flex centering on main or ensuring ReelFeed's scroll container is properly exposed.

accepted.title: Debug logging in production middleware
accepted.message: Added console.log in the auth0 middleware proxy function. This will log every proxied request with timestamp and URL to production logs, creating noise and potential performance impact.

finding.title: Leading space in className string
finding.message: The SidebarProvider className has a leading space: `className=" flex  items-center justify-center font-sans dark:bg-black"`. While browsers handle this, it's a typo that could cause issues with className manipulation libraries.
finding.evidence: <SidebarProvider className=" flex  items-center justify-center font-sans dark:bg-black">
finding.suggestion: Remove leading space: `className="flex items-center justify-center font-sans dark:bg-black"`

needsMoreContext.why: Need to see how containerRef is used internally and whether the new layout structure (nested h-full flex containers) breaks scroll detection for infinite feed loading.
To verify fetchFeed behavior and whether the layout changes affect how loading state interacts with scroll handling.
